label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is one plain upright rectangular box in every view (front, side, top, below, and the four angled views). A waist-high console would show a sloped or stepped control face, a base and a desk top, and none of that is here. The outline is clearly off the brief's words, though it is the right overall height.

M2.reason: The measured size is 24 x 24 x 40, and the height matches the 40 the brief asks for exactly (sizeOff 0). The brief gives no length or width to compare against, so the other two dimensions cannot be checked beyond that.

M3.reason: None of the console's parts are present: no dials, no two screens, no row of switches, no control face. The whole prop is one solid block.

M4.reason: The only material is a flat grey mottled stone-like surface on every face. The brief's regions (a painted metal control face, glass screens, switch and dial colours) are absent, so the required regions are missing rather than wrong in colour.

M5.reason: No surface detail is there. There are no dials, screens, switch rows, panel lines, hazard marks or wear on the console's face, and the faces are plain noise texture.

M6.reason: In the line-up it reads as a plain grey box, with nothing that marks it as a control console. A player would not take it for one of Half-Life's props, and it is the same plain block the decoy control would be.

M7.reason: There is no front to identify. A box has no console face, so the front cannot be told from the back or the sides. The model appears upright and sits on its origin, but the facing cannot be checked against the brief.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. It has 12 triangles, far under twice the Half-Life median of 62 for this size and under the third-quartile limit. The box is closed, with no open, inside-out or floating faces in the views.
